newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria OMV Q1 earnings up 8.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Austria OMV Q1 earnings up 8.5 percent.

text.p: Austrian oil firm OMV on Monday reported an 8.5 percent increase in first quarter earnings, building on last year's record result, and reiterated it expected a good profit development for the full year.
The nation's biggest industrial group posted earnings before interest and tax of 1.02 billion schillings ($84 million) in the first three months, up from 945 million a year ago.
Sales, excluding oil taxes, climbed to 21.41 billion schillings from 17.77 billion.

"The start of the 1997 business year can be called successful," OMV said in a statement. "At this point in time we can expect a positive earnings development for the current year," chief executive Richard Schenz told the annual shareholders' meeting. He did not say which earnings figures he was referring to.
OMV shares were trading 6.8 schillings down at 1,323.10 late morning having spiked to 1,338.5 schillings in early activity. Volume was moderate at 15,670 contracts.
Market participants said the results were in line with expectations.
"The only suprise was that they chose to release the figures today when there is not much going on in Vienna and the London market is closed for a holiday," a Vienna trader said.
OMV has consistently said it expects 1997 earnings to match last year's record as improved refining margins and a stronger marketing performance offset the impact of lower crude prices.

In 1996 OMV posted a net profit of 1.98 billion schillings, a pre-tax profit of 2.97 billion and earnings before interest and tax of 2.92 billion. -- Janet McBride, Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254 ($ = 12.14 Austrian Schillings)
